newsitem.title: USA: Motorola deal with Bosch seen positive.
newsitem.headline: Motorola deal with Bosch seen positive.

text.p: Motorola Inc's purchase of the mobile radio business of German automotive parts supplier Robert Bosch GmbH is a positive step and will drive further expansion in Europe for Motorola, analysts said.

"It's a good move for them, because Motorola has really been trying to expand its presence in the European market," said Mona Eraiba, an analyst for Gruntal & Co. "What they want to do is leverage their digital solution for private mobile radios."

Earlier Wednesday, Bosch said it sold its mobile radio business unit to Schaumburg, Ill-based Motorola for an undisclosed amount. The unit has annual sales of 330 million marks ($200 million) and employs almost 1,5000 workers.
The deal must still be approved by the German cartel office, Bosch said.

The unit produced technology for radio transmission between vehicles, similar to Motorola's land mobile products. Customers include fire, police and emergency services, as well as industrial and commercial businesses.
"It's a natural adjunct to the Motorola business," said Robert Gutenstein, an analyst for Kalb, Voorhis & Co. "Bosch is a great partner to have."
Analysts said this gives Motorola the ability to face off more effectively with the top European competitors, such as Swedish telecommunications group Ericsson.
Motorola previously decided to contruct a new manufacturing facility for mobile phones and increase research and development investment in three centers in Germany, the company said.
"Now you have a marketing arm and a manufacturing arm and Bosch has technology," Eraiba said.
